text:
I need an email to win back customers who cancelled. I own a home cleaning company with 18 cleaners.

What's true:
- We have 212 regular customers. 64 cancelled in the last year. In exit surveys, the most common reason was price, then a different cleaner showing up each time.
- An every-other-week cleaning for a 3-bedroom house costs $165 with us. The app services in our area charge about $140.
- Our cleaners are employees, not contractors. We pay $21 an hour and carry insurance on every visit.
- Last year 7 of our 18 cleaners left, so about 4 in 10 customers had their regular cleaner change at least once.
- We now give each customer a regular cleaner and a named backup.
- Returning customers get their first cleaning for $99.

I want the email to promise that you'll get the same cleaner every single time. Keep it to about 150 words.

Before I write, there's one problem to settle and a few gaps to fill.

**The "same cleaner every single time" promise.** Your facts don't support it. You now assign a regular cleaner *and a named backup*, which means sometimes the backup will come. Last year 7 of 18 cleaners left. If customers come back because of that promise and then get a different cleaner, you lose them a second time, and the second loss is usually for good. Here's what I'd suggest promising instead: "Your own regular cleaner every visit, and if they're ever out, a backup you already know by name." That's still a big change from what they left over, and it's true. Your $21/hour and employee status also give you an honest reason to say cleaners stay, if you'd like to use it.

A few questions:

1. **Can I use the regular-plus-named-backup wording instead of "every single time"?** If you have something that does guarantee the same person, like a policy or a refund if someone else shows up, tell me and I'll use that.
2. **What happens after the $99 first cleaning?** Does it go back to $165? Is there an expiry date or a limit on when they have to book?
3. **How should they book?** Reply to the email, a link, or a phone number?
4. **Whose name and company name go in the sign-off?** Should it come from you as the owner?
5. **Do you want to address price head-on?** I can briefly explain the $25 gap compared with the apps (employees, insurance on every visit), or I can leave price to the $99 offer.

1. Yes, use the regular cleaner plus named backup wording. I can't guarantee the same person every time because of sick days and holidays, and there's no refund policy for that. But I want the promise as strong as it can be while still being true. I can also promise no contract, and customers can cancel any time.

2. After the $99 first cleaning, it goes back to the regular $165. The offer ends December 31.

3. They can reply to the email or call 555-0164.

4. Sign it from me, Lisa Grant, owner of Brightway Home Cleaning.

5. Yes, address price briefly. I can't match $140. The app services around here mostly use contractors with no insurance on the visit.

Here's the email, at about 150 words:

<final_document>
Subject: Your own cleaner, and $99 to come back

Hi [First name],

When customers leave Brightway, they tell us two things: price, and too often a different cleaner showing up. You were right about the second, and we've fixed it.

Every customer now has their own regular cleaner, plus a named backup for sick days and holidays. If your cleaner is ever out, you'll know who's coming instead.

On price: an every-other-week cleaning for a 3-bedroom home is $165 with us, and we can't match the $140 apps. Here's why. Our cleaners are employees, not contractors, and every visit is insured. Many app services in our area use contractors and don't insure the visit.

Come back for $99 on your first cleaning, then $165 after that. No contract, and you can cancel any time. This offer ends December 31.

Reply to this email or call 555-0164 to book.

Lisa Grant
Owner, Brightway Home Cleaning
</final_document>

Some notes on the wording:
- The opening speaks about customers in general, so it doesn't claim this particular person left over price. That's because the email goes to all 64, and their reasons differ.
- I didn't mention cleaners staying longer. Seven left last year, so that claim wouldn't be safe yet.
- The line about insurance is limited to "many app services in our area." If anyone checks, that's easier to defend than a claim about all of them.
